Root cause (found this session, code-exact): for every 6s segment, _sample_keyframes (anomaly_discovery.py L45-56) routes to SemanticFrameSampler.select_keyframes (token_compressor.py L78-133), whose target K=ceil(6s*fps_sample=3.0)=18 >= the 12 frames a 2fps segment contains, so ALL ~12 ordered frames are returned — and then _comparative_call (anomaly_discovery.py L110-113) TRUNCATES to keyframes[:keyframes_per_segment], i.e. the FIRST 2 frames (t+0.0s, t+0.5s), or the first 1 (t+0.0s) under the >60-segment long-video rule. Semantic dedup only shrinks the pre-truncation pool (static segments collapse to their earliest cluster), so the VLM's evidence for each 6s segment is at best its leading ~0.5s. A brief event (RoadAccidents GT 2-3s; Shoplifting GT 2-7s, measured from the parquet) that starts mid-segment is literally never shown to the VLM — a structural CAND-MISS generator, exactly the v16 residual (Shoplifting 11/25). Mechanism: replace the first-k truncation with a deterministic uniform spread over the segment: k=2 -> frames at {t_start, t_start+3.0s}; long-video 1-kf rule -> segment midpoint. Same segment grid, same batch sizes (8x2 / 16x1), same frames/call (16), same call count, same prompts, same thresholds/merge/top-k.
